datasets.name: 5eb1f656
queryLines:
with

dim_dates as (
select
    max(concat(year,'-',month,'-01')::date ) as max_reporting_date
from
    sce_db.default.fact_electricity_synthetic_by_zip
where
    concat(year,'-',month,'-01')::date <= '2026-08-01'
)

, base_data as (
select
    (select max_reporting_date from dim_dates) as latest_date
    , concat(year,'-',month,'-01')::date as reporting_date
    , add_months(concat(year,'-',month,'-01')::date,-12)::date as py_reporting_date
    , add_months(concat(year,'-',month,'-01')::date,-1)::date as lm_reporting_date
    , *
from
    sce_db.default.fact_electricity_synthetic_by_zip
where
    concat(year,'-',month,'-01')::date <= '2026-08-01'
)



, final_data as (
select
    coalesce(cy.latest_date,py.latest_date,lm.latest_date) as latest_date
    , coalesce(cy.reporting_date,add_months(py.reporting_date,12),add_months(lm.reporting_date,1)) as reporting_date
    , coalesce(cy.zip_code,py.zip_code,lm.zip_code) as zip_code
    , coalesce(cy.is_coastal,py.is_coastal,lm.is_coastal) as is_coastal
    , coalesce(cy.seasonal_multiplier,py.seasonal_multiplier,lm.seasonal_multiplier) as seasonal_multiplier
    , cy.total_accounts
    , cy.total_kwh
    , cy.avg_kwh as average_kwh
    , cy.temperature_f as ambient_temp_f
    , cy.wildfire_tier
    -- , cy.failure_probability
    , cy.failed
    , case when cy.failed = 1 then 'Yes' else 'No' end as failed_
    , py.total_accounts as py_total_accounts
    , py.total_kwh as py_total_kwh
    , py.avg_kwh as py_average_kwh
    , py.temperature_f as py_ambient_temp_f
    , py.wildfire_tier as py_wildfire_tier
    -- , py.failure_probability as py_failure_probability
    , py.failed as py_failed
    , case when py.failed = 1 then 'Yes' else 'No' end as py_failed_
    , lm.total_accounts as lm_total_accounts
    , lm.total_kwh as lm_total_kwh
    , lm.avg_kwh as lm_average_kwh
    , lm.temperature_f as lm_ambient_temp_f
    , lm.wildfire_tier as lm_wildfire_tier
    -- , lm.failure_probability as lm_failure_probability
    , lm.failed as lm_failed
    , case when lm.failed = 1 then 'Yes' else 'No' end as lm_failed_
from
    base_data cy
    full join base_data py
        on cy.zip_code = py.zip_code
        and cy.py_reporting_date = py.reporting_date
    full join base_data lm
        on cy.zip_code = lm.zip_code
        and cy.lm_reporting_date = lm.reporting_date
)

select
    case when year(reporting_date) = year(latest_date) then 'CY' end as period_flag
    , case when reporting_date = latest_date then 'TD' end as todate_flag
    , sum(py_total_kwh) over (partition by reporting_date) as total_py_total_kwh
    , sum(lm_total_kwh) over (partition by reporting_date) as total_lm_total_kwh
    , (total_kwh - lm_total_kwh)/total_lm_total_kwh as total_accounts_cpdiff
    , (total_kwh - py_total_kwh)/total_lm_total_kwh as total_accounts_cypdiff
    , case when failed = 1 then zip_code else 'All Else' end as _zip_code_
    , *
    , case when failed = 1 then zip_code end as failed_zip_code
    , case when py_failed = 1 then zip_code end as py_failed_zip_code
    , case when lm_failed = 1 then zip_code end as lm_failed_zip_code
    , case when failed = 1 then total_accounts end as failed_total_accounts
    , case when py_failed = 1 then py_total_accounts end as py_failed_total_accounts
    , case when lm_failed = 1 then lm_total_accounts end as lm_failed_total_accounts
    , case when failed = 1 then total_kwh end as failed_total_kwh
    , case when py_failed = 1 then py_total_kwh end as py_failed_total_kwh
    , case when lm_failed = 1 then lm_total_kwh end as lm_failed_total_kwh
    , case when failed = 1 then average_kwh end as failed_average_kwh
    , case when py_failed = 1 then py_average_kwh end as py_failed_average_kwh
    , case when lm_failed = 1 then lm_average_kwh end as lm_failed_average_kwh
    , case when failed = 1 then ambient_temp_f end as failed_ambient_temp_f
    , case when py_failed = 1 then py_ambient_temp_f end as py_failed_ambient_temp_f
    , case when lm_failed = 1 then lm_ambient_temp_f end as lm_failed_ambient_temp_f
    , case when failed = 1 then wildfire_tier end as failed_wildfire_tier
    , case when py_failed = 1 then py_wildfire_tier end as py_failed_wildfire_tier
    , case when lm_failed = 1 then lm_wildfire_tier end as lm_failed_wildfire_tier
from
    final_data

columns.expression: case when count(distinct failed_zip_code) != 0 then count(distinct failed_zip_code) end/count(distinct zip_code)

datasets.name: 6addca2a
queryLines:
with

dim_dates as (
select
    max(concat(year,'-',month,'-01')::date ) as max_reporting_date
from
    sce_db.default.fact_electricity_synthetic_by_zip
where
    concat(year,'-',month,'-01')::date <= '2026-08-01'
)

, base_data as (
select
    (select max_reporting_date from dim_dates) as latest_date
    , concat(year,'-',month,'-01')::date as reporting_date
    , zip_code
    , is_coastal
    , failed
    , total_accounts
    , total_kwh
    , avg_kwh as average_kwh
    , temperature_f as ambient_temp_f
    , wildfire_tier
from
    sce_db.default.fact_electricity_synthetic_by_zip
where
    concat(year,'-',month,'-01')::date <= '2026-08-01'
)

, final_data as (
select
    latest_date
    , reporting_date
    , case when year(reporting_date) = year(latest_date) then 'CY' end as period_flag
    , case when reporting_date = latest_date then 'TD' end as todate_flag
    , case when failed = 1 then zip_code else 'Zip Codes - Not Failed' end as zip_code_grp
    , zip_code
    , case when is_coastal = true then 'Y' else 'N' end as coastal
    , failed
    , total_accounts
    , total_kwh
    , average_kwh
    , ambient_temp_f
    , wildfire_tier
    , avg(case when failed = 0 then total_accounts end) over (partition by reporting_date) as total_accounts_partitioned
    , avg(case when failed = 0 then total_kwh end) over (partition by reporting_date) as total_kwh_partitioned
    , avg(case when failed = 0 then average_kwh end) over (partition by reporting_date) as average_kwh_partitioned
    , avg(case when failed = 0 then ambient_temp_f end) over (partition by reporting_date) as ambient_temp_f_partitioned
    , avg(case when failed = 0 then wildfire_tier end) over (partition by reporting_date) as wildfire_tier_partitioned
    , total_accounts - total_accounts_partitioned as total_accounts_diff
    , total_kwh - total_kwh_partitioned as total_kwh_diff
    , average_kwh - average_kwh_partitioned as average_kwh_diff
    , ambient_temp_f - ambient_temp_f_partitioned as ambient_temp_f_diff
    , wildfire_tier - wildfire_tier_partitioned as wildfire_tier_diff
from
    base_data
)

select
    *
    , case
        -- when :metric = 'Total Accounts' then total_accounts
        when :metric = 'Total KWH' then total_kwh
        when :metric = 'Average KWH' then average_kwh
        when :metric = 'Ambient Temperature' then ambient_temp_f
        when :metric = 'Wildfire Risk' then wildfire_tier
      end as selected_metric
    , case
        -- when :metric = 'Total Accounts' then total_accounts_diff
        when :metric = 'Total KWH' then total_kwh_diff
        when :metric = 'Average KWH' then average_kwh_diff
        when :metric = 'Ambient Temperature' then ambient_temp_f_diff
        when :metric = 'Wildfire Risk' then wildfire_tier_diff
      end as metric_diff
    , case
        -- when :metric = 'Total Accounts' and total_accounts_diff <= 0  then '🟢'
        -- when :metric = 'Total Accounts' and total_accounts_diff > 0  then '🔴'
        when :metric = 'Total KWH' and total_kwh_diff <= 0  then '🟢'
        when :metric = 'Total KWH' and total_kwh_diff > 0  then '🔴'
        when :metric = 'Average KWH' and average_kwh_diff <= 0  then '🟢'
        when :metric = 'Average KWH' and average_kwh_diff > 0  then '🔴'
        when :metric = 'Ambient Temperature' and ambient_temp_f_diff <= 0  then '🟢'
        when :metric = 'Ambient Temperature' and ambient_temp_f_diff > 0  then '🔴'
        when :metric = 'Wildfire Risk' and wildfire_tier_diff <= 0  then '🟢'
        when :metric = 'Wildfire Risk' and wildfire_tier_diff > 0  then '🔴'
      end as metric_indicator
from
    final_data

    , zip_code
    , 'Test' as model_split
    , lr_pred
    , rf_pred
    , xgb_pred
    , groq_pred
from
    sce_db.default.fact_grid_vulnerabilities_by_zip_test
)

, fcst_data as (
select
    reporting_date::date as reporting_date
    , zip_code
    , 'Forecast' as model_split
    , lr_pred
    , rf_pred
    , xgb_pred
    , groq_pred
from
    sce_db.default.fact_grid_vulnerabilities_by_zip_fcst
)

, act_data as (
select
    (select max_reporting_date from dim_dates) as latest_date
    , concat(year,'-',month,'-01')::date as reporting_date
    , add_months(concat(year,'-',month,'-01')::date,-12)::date as py_reporting_date
    , add_months(concat(year,'-',month,'-01')::date,-1)::date as lm_reporting_date
    , case 
        when reporting_date < '2026-01-01' then 'Train'
        when reporting_date >= '2026-01-01' and reporting_date <= '2026-08-01' then 'Test'
        when reporting_date > '2026-08-01' then 'Forecast'
      end as model_split
    , case 
        when reporting_date <= '2026-08-01' then 'Actuals'
        when reporting_date > '2026-08-01' then 'Forecast'
      end as dataset_split
    , *
from
    sce_db.default.fact_electricity_synthetic_by_zip
)

, base_data as (
select
    a.latest_date
    , a.reporting_date
    , a.py_reporting_date
    , a.lm_reporting_date
    , a.model_split
    , a.dataset_split
    , a.zip_code
    , a.is_coastal
    , a.wildfire_tier
    , a.temperature_f
    , a.seasonal_multiplier
    , a.total_accounts
    , a.avg_kwh
    , a.total_kwh
    , a.failed
    , f.lr_pred
    , f.rf_pred
    , f.xgb_pred

    , t.rf_pred as rf_test
    , t.xgb_pred as xgb_test
    , t.groq_pred as groq_test
from
    act_data a
    left join fcst_data f
        on a.reporting_date = f.reporting_date
        and a.zip_code = f.zip_code
        and a.model_split = f.model_split
    left join test_data t
        on a.reporting_date = t.reporting_date
        and a.zip_code = t.zip_code
        and a.model_split = t.model_split
)

, final_data as (
select
    coalesce(cy.latest_date,py.latest_date,lm.latest_date) as latest_date
    , coalesce(cy.reporting_date,add_months(py.reporting_date,12),add_months(lm.reporting_date,1)) as reporting_date
    , coalesce(cy.zip_code,py.zip_code,lm.zip_code) as zip_code
    , coalesce(cy.is_coastal,py.is_coastal,lm.is_coastal) as is_coastal

    , coalesce(cy.model_split,py.model_split,lm.model_split) as model_split
    , coalesce(cy.dataset_split,py.dataset_split,lm.dataset_split) as dataset_split
    , cy.total_accounts
    , cy.total_kwh
    , cy.avg_kwh as average_kwh
    , cy.temperature_f as ambient_temp_f
    , cy.wildfire_tier
    , cy.failed
    , cy.lr_pred
    , cy.rf_pred
    , cy.xgb_pred
    , cy.groq_pred
    , cy.lr_pred as lr_test
    , cy.rf_pred as rf_test
    , cy.xgb_pred as xgb_test
    , cy.groq_pred as groq_test
    , case when cy.failed = 1 then 'Yes' else 'No' end as failed_
    , py.total_accounts as py_total_accounts
    , py.total_kwh as py_total_kwh
    , py.avg_kwh as py_average_kwh
    , py.temperature_f as py_ambient_temp_f
    , py.wildfire_tier as py_wildfire_tier
    , py.failed as py_failed
    , case when py.failed = 1 then 'Yes' else 'No' end as py_failed_
    , lm.total_accounts as lm_total_accounts
    , lm.total_kwh as lm_total_kwh
    , lm.avg_kwh as lm_average_kwh
    , lm.temperature_f as lm_ambient_temp_f
    , lm.wildfire_tier as lm_wildfire_tier
    , lm.failed as lm_failed
    , case when lm.failed = 1 then 'Yes' else 'No' end as lm_failed_
from
    base_data cy
    full join base_data py
        on cy.zip_code = py.zip_code
        and cy.py_reporting_date = py.reporting_date
    full join base_data lm
        on cy.zip_code = lm.zip_code
        and cy.lm_reporting_date = lm.reporting_date
)

select
    latest_date
    , reporting_date
    , zip_code
    , is_coastal
    , seasonal_multiplier
    , model_split
    , dataset_split
    , total_accounts
    , total_kwh
    , average_kwh
    , ambient_temp_f
    , wildfire_tier
    , failed
    , case when dataset_split = 'Actuals' then failed end as failed_act
    , case when dataset_split = 'Actuals' then failed else lr_pred end as baseline_failed
    , failed_
    , lr_pred
    , rf_pred
    , xgb_pred
    , groq_pred
    , case
        when :forecast_type = 'Logistic Regression' then lr_pred
        when :forecast_type = 'Random Forest' then rf_pred
        when :forecast_type = 'XGBoost' then xgb_pred
        when :forecast_type = 'Groq' then groq_pred

    , py_failed

    , lm_total_kwh
    , lm_average_kwh
    , lm_ambient_temp_f
    , lm_wildfire_tier
    , lm_failed
    , lm_failed_
from
    final_data
where
    year(reporting_date) = year(latest_date)

/*

lines:
Business Objective

The goal is to monitor and forecast grid failures. This dashboard provides historical trends of different inputs that may lead to grid failure. These data are also leveraged to forecast grid failures using different classification models with AI to predict grid failures by zip code.

Dashboard Views * Executive View * Grid Monitoring with Forecast * Supplemental
\* Trend Analysis
\* Grid Analysis
\* Forecast Model Evaluation
Data definitions * Zip Code - 5 digit US psotal service designation mapping the physical geographic boundary of the customers. It allows you to group data for time-series analysis and cleanly merge external spatial risk variables, such as weather, wildfire threat zones, population, etc. * Reporting Date - Reporting date at monthly frequency * Total Accounts - Total number of unique utility meters active within that specific zip code during the reporting period. This establishes the physical scale and density of the local circuit, suggesting higher account density increases base grid vulnerability, meaning single circuit failure in a high-account zip code. * Total KwH - The gross sum of all electricity consumed (in kilowatt-hours) by zip code over the entire reporting period. This represents the absolute volumetric load on the grid, which also represents systemic energy shifts across years or months to identify macro-level demand growth. * Average KwH - Calculated as total\_kwh divided by total\_accounts, this represents the mean energy intensity per customer meter. This the core proxy feature for operational grid stress. Sudden surges average\_kwh during summer months signify heavy air conditioning usage. When average intensity spikes past historic baseline thresholds, local distribution assets overheat, exponentially driving failure. * Ambient Temperature (in fahrenheit) - The localized outdoor air temperature measured at the geographical center or weather station corresponding to that specific zip code during the time. Temperature is a primary catalyst for grid asset degradation. High ambient heat severly diminishes a transformer's ability to dissipate its own internal heat. When a summer heatwave causes outdoor teperatures to spike, it triggers a compound risk effect: customer air conditioning load surges simultaneously with a drop in asset cooling capacity, pushing electrical insulation materials toward catastrophic thermal failure. * Wildlife Tier - A categorical safety classification (typically ranked from 0 to 3) representing structural environmental wildfire risk, aligned with the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) fire-threat maps. This serves as a static geographic risk weight. Overhead lines running through Tier 2 or Tier 3 zones face extreme environmental stresses like heavy winds, dry vegetation contact, and salt spray. Furthermore, during high-wind events in Tier 3 zones, SCE may proactively execute Public Safety Power Shutoffs (PSPS), which shifts electrical loads onto neighboring circuits and alters regional failure profiles.
\* Tier 0/1: low or minimal threat
\* Tier 2 (elevated): areas where there is an elevated risk for utility-associated wildfires
\* Tier 3 (high): extreme risk zones where high winds, dense fuel moisture deficits and geography create immediate danger. * Failed - A binary indicator representing whether an actual outage or asset failure occurred during the specific time step.
\* 0: Healthy / Normal operations.
\* 1: Failed / Outage event occurred.

Business Objective

The objective is to predict grid failures (by zip code) using three different classification models with AI (Groq - llama-3.3-70b-versatile and low randomness). These models optimize to reduce false negatives as it would be costly to SCE not to prevent failures for their customers. In other words, we highly penalize predictions that do not classify predictions correctly for failed grids by conducting a training-test validation using time-series data discussed in the Readme tab of this dashboard. We then leverage these different classification models to predict grid failure through Dec. 2026. Classification Models and Assumptions We use three classification models that assumes predictions are based on linear assumptions (logistic regression) and non-linear assumptions (random forest and XGBoost). Three models and their results are then used within an AI skills environment to triangulate grid failure predictions, as well as evaluate model performance. We find that Logistic Regression and AI Groq predict more grid failures in which there is an increase in false positives based on training-test validation while ensuring we minimize false negatives. This may be a result of linear assumptions and AI using these conservative results to predict more grid failures. In addition, we most likely need to adjust the AI prompting with better contextual information. Lastly, we not that standard balancing techniques were not used to account for rare cases such as grid failures when using time-series data. * Logistic Regression (Baseline) * Random Forest * XGBoost * AI Groq Data Data are described in Readme and we consider lag variables to improve time-series predictions. We have data from 2024-2026 and split the data into training data between 2024-Jan to 2025-Dec with a test data between 2026-Jan to 2026-Aug. Then we forecast failures from 2026-Sept to 2026-Dec. * Zip Code * Reporting Date * Average KwH * Ambient Temperature (in fahrenheit) * Wildlife Tier - * Failed (target) Results In the training-test validation phase (training, we gather the following results: * Logistic regression: Test validation shows we were able to predict all 71 failures correctly with 17 false positives. * Random forest: Test validation show we were able to predict all 71 failures correctly with 7 false positives. * XGBoost: Test Validation show we were able to predict all 71 failures correctly with 2 false positives. * AI Groq: Test Validation shows we were able to predict all 71 failures correctly with 17 false positives. All AUCs are above 0.99. The results show that logistic regression and AI Groq are the most conservative in terms of considering more failure rates, while Random Forest and XGBoost are the most accurate in terms of prediction.
